correctness.rationale: The n−1 simple-root edge differences are a basis of the intrinsic Euclidean hyperplane sum x_i=0. Their ± convex hull is a crosspolytope with facet dual normals x^ε satisfying consecutive coordinate gaps ε_i. The zero-sum variance identity gives ||x^ε||²=(1/n)sum_{p<q}(sum_{k=p}^{q−1}ε_k)² ≤ n(n²−1)/12, with equality only the two constant sign patterns for n≥3 (and the two choices for n=2). Opposite tight facets bound every ball globally, so r=√[12/(n(n²−1))]; centers are exactly the stated hyperplane section and slack halfspaces, with relative dimension n−2, including zero-dimensional n=2. Opposite vertices of norm √2 force unique circumsphere center zero. Independently enumerated all sign vectors in small dimensions, confirming exactly two tight normals; proof itself is all n.
